Abstract Background Chordoma is a locally aggressive bone tumor with a high capability of recurrence. Because chordoma often occurs at critical locations next to neurovascular structures, there is an urgent need to introduce validated biomarkers. T ‐ box transcription factor T ( TBXT ; OMIM: 601397) plays an important role in the pathogenesis and survival of chordoma cells. Methods Herein, we aimed to show whether rs2305089 polymorphism is correlated with chordoma in the Iranian population. In order to detect rs2305089, tetra‐primer amplification refractory mutation system‐polymerase chain reaction (T‐ARMS‐PCR) was used. In total, 19 chordoma patients and 108 normal healthy individuals were recruited and screened using T‐ARMS‐PCR. The results were subsequently validated by Sanger sequencing. Results The genotype distributions and allele frequencies were significantly different among the patient and healthy groups ( p ‐value <0.05). The A allele of rs2305089 showed a significant positive association with chordoma risk ( p ‐value <0.05). DNA sequencing verified the T‐ARMS‐PCR results as well. This study demonstrated the association between TBXT rs2305089 and chordoma in an Iranian population using a simple, accurate, and cost‐effective T‐ARMS‐PCR assay. Conclusions Our results were in line with those of previous studies showing that TBXT rs2305089 is associated with chordoma development. We also developed an efficient T‐ARMS‐PCR assay to determine the genotype of rs2305089. This study aimed to show whether rs2305089 polymorphism is associated with chordoma in the Iranian population. J Clin Lab Anal . 2022 ; 36 : e24150 . doi: 10.1002/jcla.24150 1 INTRODUCTION Chordoma (OMIM: 215400) is a rare primary bone tumor that originated from notochord remnants—a rod‐like structure that supports embryo development—in the axial skeleton. 1 , 2 , 3 Chordoma usually progresses slowly, but its locally aggressive nature can affect the patients’ quality of life. 4 This kind of cancer often occurs sporadically, but some rare familial cases have also been documented. 5 The estimated overall incidence of chordoma in the general population is 0.08 per 100,000 live births. 4 This cancer affects males more frequently than females (2:1). 6 Although chordoma's occurrence has been reported from infancy to senescence, it often occurs in the sixth decade of patients’ life. 2 Furthermore, its occurrence tends to be higher in Caucasians than in African‐Americans (4:1). 2 The first‐line strategies to treat primary chordoma are still based on surgical resection followed by radiotherapy, although these strategies result in a median overall survival of 7.7 years. 7 , 8 Moreover, chordoma, as a mildly aggressive cancer, often affects the adjacent vital tissues before becoming symptomatic—thus, completely resecting all cancer‐related tissues is demanding. In short, there is an urgent need to introduce safe biomarkers (e.g., susceptible genetic loci) to better manage patients as accurately as possible. TBXT ( T ‐ box transcription factor T ; OMIM: 601397) has been introduced as one of the most important genes in embryonic development. This gene is exclusively expressed during the early stages of development and is silenced in most developed tissues, except differentiated tissues of the testis and some parts of the thyroid. 9 , 10 TBXT —also known as the T gene or brachyury—functions as an embryonic nuclear transcription factor in mesoderm formation and differentiation. This protein binds to the palindromic T‐site of DNA using its N‐terminus (T‐box). 11 Interestingly, Tbxt −/− mice die during the embryonic period due to multiple mesodermal abnormalities. 11 The TBXT is located on the 6q27 region and is associated with susceptibility to chordoma and neural tube defects. 5 , 9 , 12 , 13 For example, the homozygous H171R was observed in four members of three unrelated consanguineous families with sacral agenesis and vertebral anomalies. 14 Germline duplication of TBXT was also observed in the familial type of chordoma. 5 Moreover, the silencing of TBXT in chordoma cell line U‐CH1 resulted in decreased cell proliferation. 12 Pillay et al. indicated a strong association between chordoma risk and the common nonsynonymous single‐nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) rs2305089 in Europeans. 1 Rs2305089 (NM_003181.4; c.530G>A: p. Gly177Asp) is located at exon 4 of TBXT . The researchers also indicated a higher mRNA expression of TBXT in patients with AA genotype than in GA sporadic chordoma patients without TBXT gene duplication. 1 The higher susceptibility imputed to the A allele to chordoma was later confirmed by Kelley et al. in American and Canadian individuals. 3 On the contrary, a study using 65 skull‐based chordoma patients and 120 healthy individuals among the Chinese population showed that rs2305089 was not significantly correlated with chordoma risk. 15 Since the reported association of rs2305089 may be linked to ‘population‐specific’ backgrounds, it is imperative to check this association in different ethnic populations. Hence, finding disorder‐associated alleles/genotypes is important to reduce the burden of genetic disorders and take steps toward turning ‘generalized’ medicine into ‘personalized’ medicine. Although using high‐throughput approaches (e.g., genome‐wide association studies, TaqMan genotyping assay, and whole‐exome sequencing) is highly suggested for genetic association study, they are not cost‐affordable for limited resources. Such techniques, in some cases, can be replaced by inexpensive, simple, and quick ones, such as tetra‐primer amplification refractory mutation system‐polymerase chain reaction (T‐ARMS‐PCR). T‐ARMS‐PCR amplifies the specific target template by only two sets of primers, including inner and outer ones. The outer primers are non‐allele‐specific and simply amplify the target sequences of the main template, whereas the inner primers are allele‐specific ones whose 3′‐ends embrace the polymorphic nucleotides. The present study investigated the association between TBXT rs2305089 polymorphism and chordoma in an Iranian population. Herein, we also aimed to develop a reliable, low‐cost, and simple T‐ARMS‐PCR method to ease the genotyping of this polymorphism.

core_effect_and_quantification.biomarker_name: rs2305089 polymorphism (A allele and AA genotype)
core_effect_and_quantification.magnitude_quantification: p-value <0.05; A allele OR=2.59 (95% CI: 1.2–5.4, p=0.011) with 71% frequency in patients vs 49% in controls; AA genotype OR=4.1 (95% CI: 1.5–11, p=0.004)

core_effect_and_quantification.activity_context: overall survival in spinal column chordoma patients

molecular_mechanism_and_relationship.activity_type_context: chordoma pathogenesis, susceptibility, development, and survival
molecular_mechanism_and_relationship.mechanism_description: The T-box transcription factor T (TBXT) gene, containing the rs2305089 SNP, is crucial for mesoderm formation and notochord development, functioning as an embryonic nuclear transcription factor. In chordoma, TBXT expression is aberrantly upregulated, promoting cell migration, invasion, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) by altering mesenchymal and epithelial markers. The A allele of rs2305089 is located in the conserved DNA-binding domain and is associated with higher mRNA expression of TBXT, particularly in patients with the AA genotype, potentially decreasing protein stability and leading to increased expression of downstream targets. TBXT is considered a therapeutic target, with potential for small molecule inhibitors or immunotherapy.

dose_intensity_and_specificity.dose_comparison_summary: No explicit dose-response relationship was detailed. The association of rs2305089 is not influenced by patient age or tumor location, though allele frequencies can vary by population. The study focused on genetic association rather than dose-response.
dose_intensity_and_specificity.specificity_finding: The association of rs2305089 with chordoma risk exhibits population-specific variability; it was strongly associated in European, American, Canadian, and Iranian populations, but not significantly correlated in a Chinese population. TBXT expression itself is a specific diagnostic hallmark of chordoma, showing low expression in normal adult tissues but cancer-specific expression. The T-ARMS-PCR method developed for genotyping rs2305089 demonstrated high sensitivity, specificity, and 100% concordance with DNA sequencing.

clinical_implication_and_population.target_population: Iranian chordoma patients and healthy controls, with findings suggesting population-specific relevance. The biomarker is also relevant to general chordoma patient populations, including those with spinal column chordoma.
clinical_implication_and_population.health_implication: Rs2305089 is a susceptible genetic locus associated with increased chordoma risk and development. TBXT, the gene containing this SNP, is a definitive diagnostic biomarker and a potential therapeutic target. Interestingly, the A variant of rs2305089 was also associated with significantly improved overall survival in spinal column chordoma patients. This polymorphism offers an effective screening method, potentially leading to new molecular targeted therapies, improved diagnosis, management, and genetic counseling for chordoma patients.
clinical_implication_and_population.risk_classification: The A allele and AA genotype of rs2305089 are classified as adverse risk factors for chordoma development. Conversely, the A variant of rs2305089 shows a protective benefit in terms of improved overall survival for spinal column chordoma patients. Overall, rs2305089 provides diagnostic utility for identifying disorder-associated alleles and genotypes, and TBXT itself is recognized as a therapeutic target.

biomarker_reliability_and_future_focus.reliability_assessment: The developed T-ARMS-PCR assay for genotyping rs2305089 is highly reliable, described as simple, easy, quick, accurate, sensitive, specific, and cost-effective. Its results were validated by Sanger sequencing, showing 100% concordance and complete consistency. This method is more affordable and does not require specialized expensive tools compared to other SNP detection techniques. The study's data were fully consistent with previous findings, supporting the conclusions.
recommended_alternatives: Polymerase chain reaction-restriction fragment length polymorphism (PCR-RFLP)
